faqModal.description:
These FAQs refer exclusively to the user area of the Kulturkataster, i.e., to topics concerning accounts and maintaining data.
General questions about the purpose and benefits of the Kulturkataster, the scope of the different versions, and the methodological approach can be found in the “Info & Service” area of the Kulturkataster.
The FAQs are continuously updated and expanded; if your question does not yet appear here, please feel free to email the editorial team at info@kulturkataster.berlin.

question1.answer: When you are logged in, you can change your account details in the Kulturkataster Portal via the gear icon in the upper left. There you can update, for example, your name, email address, or password. If you would like to change your password, you first need to enter your current password and can then set a new password.
question1.title: How can I change my account details?

question10.answer: You can download a list of cultural locations by clicking the downward arrow icon in the left-hand menu (the second icon from the top). Before downloading, you must confirm that you have read and agreed to the data usage agreement and the legal notices. Before starting the download, you can filter or sort the data displayed on the map. Clicking the download icon will export the currently displayed selection. Data can be exported in XLS, XLSX, or CSV format. The downloaded dataset reflects both the information currently visible in the Kulturkataster and the access rights associated with your user account. By downloading the data, you agree not to share it with third parties and to use it only in accordance with applicable legal requirements -particularly the GDPR where personal data is involved- and solely for the purposes of the Kulturkataster. The purposes of the Kulturkataster are non-commercial. They include systematic collection, structuring, and public provision of data on places of cultural production and use throughout the State of Berlin. The aim is to establish a reliable data foundation for cultural policy decisions, cultural urban development, and collaboration between cultural stakeholders, public administration, academia, and the wider public.
question10.title: How does the data download work?

question11.answer: The FAQs are continuously updated and expanded. If your question is not answered here yet, please send the editorial team an email at: info@kulturkataster.berlin
question11.title: I still have a question. Who can I contact?

question2.answer: You can delete your user account yourself at any time in the Kulturkataster Portal. When you are logged in, you can find this option via the gear icon in the upper left. After deletion, the personal data associated with your account will be removed from the system. However, changes, additions, or new cultural locations that you submitted for inclusion in the Kulturkataster and that have already been adopted editorially will not automatically be deleted. If you would like a cultural location, or specific data about a cultural location, to be removed from the Kulturkataster, please send an email with a brief explanation to: info@kulturkataster.berlin. The editorial team will review your request and then get back to you.
question2.title: How can I have my account deleted, and what happens to my data?

question3.answer: Yes, a cultural location can be assigned to several users in the Kulturkataster Portal. This means, for example, that several people who officially work for or are responsible for the same cultural location can receive access to that cultural location and submit change proposals. In addition, authorized employees of a network or association, a Berlin district, or the State of Berlin may also receive viewing and collaboration rights for cultural locations. Collaboration in the Kulturkataster is therefore intentionally designed to be cooperative. All changes are reviewed by the editorial team before publication.
question3.title: Can several users manage a cultural location?

question4.answer:
In principle, anyone aged 18 or over may create an account in the Kulturkataster. 
Accounts are particularly worthwhile for staff members of cultural locations, public administration, or networks/associations who would like to contribute to and maintain data on a regular basis. If you only want to submit change or addition proposals once or occasionally, guest access is a good choice.
question4.title: Who can create an account, and what are the benefits of an account over guest access?

question5.answer: After registering, you will receive an email asking you to confirm your email address. Once your address has been confirmed, your account will be activated and you will be able to log in to the Kulturkataster Portal. If you indicate during registration that you work for a Berlin district, the State of Berlin, a network, or an association, the editorial team will verify this information. Only after this review can the appropriate viewing and contribution permissions be assigned to your account. The editorial team aims to process requests as quickly as possible.
question5.title: When will my account be activated?

question6.answer: Once you are logged in, you will find the "Cultural Locations" section in the Kulturkataster Portal. Click the plus (+) icon to propose a new cultural location for inclusion in the Kulturkataster. If a cultural location is already listed, you can request that it be linked to your account by selecting "Claim My Locations." Once approved, the cultural location will appear in your personal overview and you will have access to additional data. All new entries and proposed changes are reviewed by the editorial team before publication.
question6.title: How can I create a new cultural location or link an existing cultural location to my account?

question7.answer: All information submitted through a user account or via guest access is reviewed by the editorial team before publication. This applies equally to new cultural locations and to changes or additions to existing entries, regardless of whether the submission comes from individual users, employees of a Berlin district, the State of Berlin, or a network or association. Submissions are not published automatically. They are only published after editorial review. The editorial team aims to process submissions as quickly as possible.
question7.title: When and how is the data I submit published?

question8.answer: If you have forgotten your password, click "Forgot Password" on the login page. You will automatically receive an email containing a link that allows you to create a new password. If you are already logged in and wish to change your password, open the Kulturkataster Portal and click the gear icon in the top-left corner. You will first be asked to enter your current password before choosing a new one.
question8.title: What should I do if I have forgotten my password or want to change it?

question9.answer: Users indicate during registration whether they are employees of a network or association, a Berlin district, or the State of Berlin. If none of these options applies, they select “No.” For users who indicate that they work for a district administration or the state administration, KRB reviews after registration whether there is a professional connection to cultural or urban development topics. This review is carried out at KRB’s discretion. Employees of networks and associations who can provide proof that they are elected representatives, commissioned freelancers, or full-time or part-time employees of the respective network or association may receive permissions to view, contribute to, or download data, including sensitive data. As a minimum requirement, the relevant email address must clearly identify the affiliation. KRB determines at its discretion whether this requirement has been met.

bodySections: **In a growing metropolis like Berlin, spaces for art and culture are scarce resources. Displacement, competition for spaces and location are a threat to the cultural spaces in Berlin, which play a diverse and critical role for the city. They are a location factor, tourism magnet and motor for innovation, they serve the transfer of knowledge, have a memorial function and support community by forming a framework for identity for a diverse and inclusive civic society. The Kulturkataster, an inventory of Berlin’s cultural landscape on a digital map that is freely accessible online, is a decisive step in the direction of sustainable cultural urban development.**

The Kulturkataster was mentioned in the guidelines of the governmental policy the current legislative period. At the end of 2022, Kulturraum Berlin gGmbH (KRB) was entrusted with the conceptualization by Berlin’s Senate Department for Culture and Community and presented the starting situation and needs as well as a realization concept for the Kulturkataster in two concept papers (realized by the Studio für unendliche Möglichkeiten). The realization in 2024 was also assigned to KRB. KRB, in turn, tasked Technologiestiftung Berlin with the development of the online-based map application.
## The framework for the development of the Kulturkataster is formed by four cultural policy guidelines that KRB has elaborated with Berlin’s Senate Department for Culture and Community:

1. Evidence-based cultural policy and cultural urban development: The Berlin Kulturkataster creates a comprehensive data basis about cultural spaces in order to allow the creation of fact-based cultural policy and targeted urban development.
2. The protection as well as new development of spaces for culture: The Kulturkataster serves as an instrument for a sustainable monitoring of cultural areas in order to support their preservation and to develop new spaces.
3. The fair distribution of cultural offerings throughout the city and equal opportunities in terms of participation: The Kulturkataster visualizes gaps in cultural offerings and supports urban planning in creating balanced and fair cultural offerings for all Berliners.
4. The improvement of the cooperation between departments, levels and sectors: As a flexible digital planning instrument, the Kulturkataster strengthens the cooperation between the different areas of responsibility, departmental levels as well as Berlin’s entire cultural community.

The Berlin Kulturkataster has been created to create a record of a cultural landscape that is more diverse, dynamic and interdisciplinary than any other. As much as the editorial team wishes that this was not the case, this process can never be completed. This is why a stated goal of the project is to continuously approximate a current state of Berlin’s cultural landscape on the digital map. This can only be achieved in cooperation with those for whom the Kulturkataster can be an important tool – the administrators on the district and state levels in  Berlin, the numerous advocacy groups for the artistic disciplines, academics, experts, activists and, of course, the cultural locations themselves.

A broad idea of the term culture and a descriptive understanding of culture form the foundations of the Kulturkataster. The database has registered a large number of locations. Additional categories and cultural locations will follow in the next versions. Instead of assessing cultural forms of expression, these are described and sorted in the Kulturkataster according to numerous criteria. This values the individual contributions that both the individual locations as well entire disciplines contribute to the cultural framework of the city.
`documentation-card`

The development of Berlin’s Kulturkataster takes place as a learning process. This means that new versions of the Kulturkataster will be published at fixed intervals. The future versions are intended to make new functionalities and updated information available. This process allows the project team to integrate suggestions and criticism into the ongoing development process and invites the users of the Kulturkataster to actively participate in its future orientation.

accordion.answer:
Our editorial team is committed to mapping all cultural locations in Berlin. However, this is an ongoing process that will never be fully complete. Many categories have not yet been included (e.g. archives, public art, artist residencies, or cultural organizations). In addition, some existing categories still contain gaps (e.g. private galleries and private art schools), which will be addressed in future updates.
If you cannot find a cultural location, you can submit it using the “Contribute” form. On the desktop version, click the pencil icon in the left-hand navigation. On a tablet or smartphone, tap the pencil icon in the bottom-right corner and follow the instructions.
accordion.question: Why is my cultural location not listed in the Kulturkataster?

accordion.answer: You can add or correct information for existing cultural locations, or suggest new ones for inclusion in the Kulturkataster. This can be done either through guest access (without an account) or with your own user account. You can find the section for contributing data via the pencil icon in the menu on the left.
accordion.question: How can I add or correct information about a cultural location?

accordion.answer:
Please note that submissions to the Kulturkataster are not published automatically. Every submission is reviewed individually by the editorial team.
We appreciate your patience, as this review process may take some time. In some cases, subject-matter experts are consulted before a decision is made. If we require any additional information, we will contact you by email.
accordion.question: I submitted my cultural location, but it still does not appear on the map. Why?

accordion.answer:
The Kulturkataster continues to grow with each new version. The project team deliberately began with a small selection of specialist maps from the Berlin Geoportal and will integrate additional maps based on users' recommendations.
We welcome your suggestions. Please send them to: [info@kulturkataster.berlin](mailto:info@kulturkataster.berlin).
accordion.question: Why does the Kulturkataster include only a limited number of specialist maps from the Berlin Geoportal?

accordion.answer:
At this stage, the Kulturkataster does not offer users the ability to manage their own entries independently.
If you would like your cultural location to be removed, please contact our editorial team. We will delete your entry as quickly as possible.
Please email: [info@kulturkataster.berlin](mailto:info@kulturkataster.berlin).
accordion.question: How can I have my cultural location removed from the Kulturkataster?

accordion.answer: In principle, anyone aged 18 or over may create an account in the Kulturkataster. Accounts are particularly worthwhile for staff members of cultural locations, public administration, or networks/associations who would like to contribute to and maintain data on a regular basis. If you only want to submit change or addition proposals once or occasionally, guest access is a good choice.
accordion.question: Who can create an account, and what are the benefits of an account over guest access?

accordion.answer:
After registering, you will receive an email asking you to confirm your email address. Once your address has been confirmed, your account will be activated and you will be able to log in to the Kulturkataster Portal.
If you indicate during registration that you work for a Berlin district, the State of Berlin, a network, or an association, the editorial team will verify this information. Only after this review can the appropriate viewing and contribution permissions be assigned to your account.
The editorial team aims to process requests as quickly as possible.
accordion.question: When will my account be activated?

accordion.answer:
Once you are logged in, you will find the "Cultural Locations" section in the Kulturkataster Portal.
Click the plus (+) icon to propose a new cultural location for inclusion in the Kulturkataster.
If a cultural location is already listed, you can request that it be linked to your account by selecting "Claim My Locations."
Once approved, the cultural location will appear in your personal overview and you will have access to additional data.
All new entries and proposed changes are reviewed by the editorial team before publication.
accordion.question: How can I create a new cultural location or link an existing cultural location to my account?

accordion.answer:
All information submitted through a user account or via guest access is reviewed by the editorial team before publication.
This applies equally to new cultural locations and to changes or additions to existing entries, regardless of whether the submission comes from individual users, employees of a Berlin district, the State of Berlin, or a network or association.
Submissions are not published automatically. They are only published after editorial review.
The editorial team aims to process submissions as quickly as possible.
accordion.question: When and how is the data I submit published?

accordion.answer:
If you have forgotten your password, click "Forgot Password" on the login page. You will automatically receive an email containing a link that allows you to create a new password.
If you are already logged in and wish to change your password, open the Kulturkataster Portal and click the gear icon in the top-left corner. You will first be asked to enter your current password before choosing a new one.
accordion.question: What should I do if I have forgotten my password or want to change it?

accordion.answer:
Users indicate during registration whether they are employees of a network or association, a Berlin district, or the State of Berlin. If none of these options applies, they select “No.” For users who indicate that they work for a district administration or the state administration, KRB reviews after registration whether there is a professional connection to cultural or urban development topics. This review is carried out at KRB’s discretion.
Employees of networks and associations who can provide proof that they are elected representatives, commissioned freelancers, or full-time or part-time employees of the respective network or association may receive permissions to view, contribute to, or download data, including sensitive data. As a minimum requirement, the relevant email address must clearly identify the affiliation. KRB determines at its discretion whether this requirement has been met.
accordion.question: What are the requirements for obtaining an account as a public administration employee or as an employee of a network or association?

accordion.answer:
You can download a list of cultural locations by clicking the downward arrow icon in the left-hand menu (the second icon from the top).
Before downloading, you must confirm that you have read and agreed to the data usage agreement and the legal notices.
Before starting the download, you can filter or sort the data displayed on the map. Clicking the download icon will export the currently displayed selection.
Data can be exported in XLS, XLSX, or CSV format.
The downloaded dataset reflects both the information currently visible in the Kulturkataster and the access rights associated with your user account.
By downloading the data, you agree not to share it with third parties and to use it only in accordance with applicable legal requirements -particularly the GDPR where personal data is involved- and solely for the purposes of the Kulturkataster.
The purposes of the Kulturkataster are non-commercial. They include systematic collection, structuring, and public provision of data on places of cultural production and use throughout the State of Berlin. The aim is to establish a reliable data foundation for cultural policy decisions, cultural urban development, and collaboration between cultural stakeholders, public administration, academia, and the wider public.

**Since July 2026, Version 2 of the Berlin Kulturkataster has been available, offering an expanded version of our digital platform—a shared workspace for cultural locations, associations, and public administration. The Kulturkataster systematically documents Berlin's cultural landscape and is continuously being developed.**

Below you will find an overview of the key features and content included in the current version. The next development stage is planned for the end of 2026 and will expand the Kulturkataster with additional cultural location categories, updated data, and a scientifically based Cultural Location Index.\
You can help us improve the Kulturkataster. Use the [link](/institution) to submit missing cultural locations and suggest changes to existing entries.\
**If you have suggestions or feedback, please contact us at:** [info@kulturkataster.berlin](mailto:info@kulturkataster.berlin)\
The current release of the Kulturkataster is Version 2.

## Version 2 Overview
**Features already included from Version 1**
- {{count}} cultural locations with basic information (name, full address, general contact details, funding and financing information)
- 16 categories and 76 subcategories
- Integration of 12 specialist maps from the Berlin Geoportal
- A search function that allows you to search for addresses and the names of cultural locations.
- A filter that enables you to search by district, category, and subcategory. You can also choose to display closed cultural locations. 
- Information available in German Sign Language and Plain Language 
- An accessible list view 

**New Features in Version 2**
- Login area for registered users 
- Collaborative data management by cultural locations, networks, associations, and public administration through the integrated “Contribute” feature 
- Editing and updating cultural location data by authorized users 
- Updated download function for publicly available data 
- English-language user interface and content 

**Planned Additions by the End of 2026**
- Updated content in German Sign Language 
- Updated content in Plain Language 
- Additional cultural location categories 
- A scientifically based Cultural Location Index

`image-text-card|/resources/bedienung/1_Bewegen.jpg|left|Move the Map|On a computer: Click and hold the left mouse button, then drag the map in the desired direction.\nOn a smartphone or tablet: Touch the screen with one finger and swipe across the map.`

`image-text-card|/resources/bedienung/2_Zoom.jpg|right|Zoom|On a computer: Use the mouse wheel or the plus (+) and minus (-) buttons in the bottom-right corner of the screen.\nOn a smartphone or tablet: Place two fingers on the screen and move them apart to zoom in. `image-text-card|/resources/bedienung/3_Suche.jpg|left|Search for a Location|On a computer: Open the search field by clicking the magnifying glass icon in the top-left corner.\nOn a smartphone or tablet: Open the search field by tapping the magnifying glass icon at the bottom of the screen. `image-text-card|/resources/bedienung/4_Filter.jpg|right|Use Filters|You can filter all cultural locations by district, category and subcategory.\nOn a computer: Open the filter panel by tapping the icon with the three horizontal lines in the top-left corner.\nOn a smartphone or tablet: Open the filter panel by tapping the icon with the three horizontal lines in the top-left corner.\nBy default, only open cultural locations are displayed on the map. To also display temporarily or permanently closed cultural locations, activate the “Show Closed Locations” option.`

`image-text-card|/resources/bedienung/5_Download.jpg|left|Download a Selection|The Kulturkataster allows you to download information for individual cultural locations or for all cultural locations currently displayed in your map view.\nOn a computer: Click the downward arrow in the left-hand navigation panel.\nOn a smartphone or tablet: Tap the downward arrow in the bottom-right navigation menu.`

`image-text-card|/resources/bedienung/6_Mitwirken.jpg|right|Submit a Cultural Location|On a computer: Open the "Contribute" form by clicking the pencil icon in the top-left corner.\nOn a smartphone or tablet: Open the "Contribute" form by tapping the pencil icon in the bottom-right corner.\nFollow the instructions in the form and complete all fields carefully. ## Preamble

Kulturraum Berlin gGmbH, represented by Dirk Förster (Managing Director), Spandauer Damm 19, 14059 Berlin (hereinafter “KRB”), implements the Kulturkataster project, a platform containing data on cultural locations. The project is funded by Berlin’s Senate Department for Culture and Community.
## Definitions

### 1.1 Kulturkataster

The Kulturkataster is a browser-based platform containing data on places relevant to cultural urban development. The purpose of the Kulturkataster is the systematic collection, structuring and public provision of data on places of cultural production and use in the State of Berlin, in order to create a reliable data basis for cultural policy decisions, cultural urban development and cooperation between cultural actors, administration, academia and the public. The Kulturkataster is openly accessible, records places of cultural production and use, makes them publicly visible and supports cultural actors, administration and policymakers in developing and safeguarding cultural locations.

### 1.2 Kulturraum Berlin gGmbH (KRB)

KRB is the operator of the Kulturkataster.

### 1.3 Cultural Location

Cultural locations are places used for cultural purposes in the State of Berlin at which cultural productions, presentations or uses take place or have taken place and which are recorded, or are intended to be recorded, in the Kulturkataster.

### 1.4 Sensitive and Non-Sensitive Data

The Kulturkataster records data on cultural locations. A distinction is made between

- non-sensitive data, which are visible to all users regardless of registration, and
- sensitive data, which become visible only after registration and only after KRB has assigned the respective access rights (see Section 2).

#### 1.4.1 Non-Sensitive Data

Name of the cultural location, umbrella organization, type of financing, type of funding, general email address, public telephone number, website, cultural area, address with geoposition, usage status, protection status, type of owner, organizational form, period during which the cultural location has existed at the location, willingness to receive space requests, description of spaces/areas, available for target group/discipline, contact information for space requests, equipment, time availability, accessibility, costs, status, data source (where the data comes from), additional information that is publicly accessible or that does not appear to be subject to any restriction on disclosure under law or contract.

#### 1.4.2 Sensitive Data

Size of the usable area (m²), number of work spaces, capacity (persons), detailed information on protection status, owner of the property, end of contract, form of contract, reasons for closing, private location information: contact person’s first name, contact person’s last name, contact person’s email address, contact person’s telephone number, internal notes.
## Registration

### 2.1 Users 

Users are natural persons who use the Kulturkataster either with or without registration.

### 2.2 Registration and Discretionary Review

Users who register state during registration whether they are staff members of a network or association, a Berlin district administration or the State of Berlin. If none of these options apply, users select “No”.
When information is provided regarding work for district administrations or state administrations, KRB checks after registration whether there is a professional connection to cultural or urban development matters. This review is carried out at KRB’s own discretion.

Staff members of networks and associations who can prove that they are elected representatives, commissioned freelancers or full-time or part-time employees of the relevant network or association are also granted access, participation or download rights for sensitive data. At a minimum, a corresponding email address must be attributable to the relevant network or association. Whether such a connection exists is reviewed by KRB at its own discretion.

### 2.3 Confirmation Prior to Submission

Before submitting the registration request, the user confirms that they have taken note of these KRB Terms of Use and decides whether to subscribe voluntarily to the newsletter (double opt-in procedure).

![Registration form with confirmation of the Terms of Use and newsletter selection](/resources/terms_en_1.png)
## Access Rights, Contributions, Download

### 3.1 Access Rights to Non-Sensitive Data

Non-sensitive data are visible to all users, with or without registration.

### 3.2 Access Rights to Sensitive Data

After registration, KRB assigns registered users access rights in relation to sensitive data of cultural locations. This assignment is based on the information on affiliation provided during registration. If “no” affiliation is indicated, KRB does not initially assign any access rights in relation to sensitive data of cultural locations.

KRB distinguishes between the following access rights that may be assigned to users:
#### 3.2.1 Access Rights in Relation to Sensitive Data of All Cultural Locations in a District

#### 3.2.2 Access Rights in Relation to Sensitive Data of All Cultural Locations in the State of Berlin

Within district administrations and state administrations, administrative staff are granted access, participation or download rights for sensitive data by KRB only if there is a professional connection to cultural or urban development matters. Whether such a connection exists is reviewed by KRB at its own discretion.
#### 3.2.3 Access Rights in Relation to Sensitive Data of Cultural Locations Individually Assigned by KRB to an Arts-Sector Association

#### 3.2.4 Access Rights in Relation to Sensitive Data of Cultural Locations Individually Assigned by KRB to Registered Users

Users who indicate “no” affiliation during registration (see Section 2 above) may use the “Claim My Locations” button to apply to KRB for an individual assignment of a cultural location. KRB reviews the application and decides whether to assign the cultural location to the user. 

If a cultural location has been individually assigned to a user in this way, the user has access to the sensitive data of that cultural location. Without such individual assignment, users who have not indicated an affiliation have no access to sensitive data of cultural locations. Like unregistered users, they may view the non-sensitive data of all cultural locations.

### 3.3 Contributions by Users

Registered and unregistered users may contribute to the Kulturkataster. They have the option, via the “Contribute” button, to
#### 3.3.1 Propose a New Cultural Location for Entry,

#### 3.3.2 Propose Additions or Changes in Relation to an Existing Cultural Location.

KRB reviews every contribution by users and, following its review, decides on publication of the contribution in the Kulturkataster.

### 3.4 Data Download

Registered users may download the data corresponding to their assigned access rights, i.e. non-sensitive data and sensitive data that they are able to view.

The data made available for download may be processed, used and edited by users for non-commercial publications and may be used only in accordance with legal requirements, in particular the GDPR where personal data are concerned, and only in line with the purposes described in these Terms of Use (see Definitions, Section 1.1).

In particular, personal data may not be further processed, published or passed on to third parties without a legal basis.
## Data Collection and Maintenance

### 7.1 Collection of the Data

The collection of data in the Kulturkataster is based on data researched by KRB itself or provided through contributions by users.

#### 7.1.1 KRB Data and Research by the KRB Editorial Team

KRB may independently create and maintain data on cultural locations. For this purpose, the KRB editorial team may research data from generally accessible sources as well as from other sources and include them in the Kulturkataster.

#### 7.1.2 Data from Contributions by Users

Users may submit suggestions for changes or additions via the “Contribute” button in the left-hand bar or in their own account, as illustrated below.

![Contribute button in the Kulturkataster](/resources/terms_en_2.png)

Contributions may relate to the following content:

##### 7.1.2.1 Additions to Existing Data

Users may propose additions or changes to existing data, in particular to non-sensitive data or - where access rights have been assigned - to sensitive data of cultural locations.

##### 7.1.2.2 Submission of New Cultural Locations

Users may submit suggestions for including new cultural locations in the Kulturkataster by transmitting the data provided for this purpose via the Kulturkataster.

##### 7.1.2.3 Submission of Sensitive Data

Users may submit sensitive data on cultural locations.
KRB reviews all contributions as part of editorial data maintenance (see the following section) and decides on publication.

### 7.2 Editorial Maintenance of the Data by the KRB Editorial Team

Suggestions are not published automatically, but only after a decision by KRB.

#### 7.2.1 Editorial Review and Decision on Publication or Rejection

All details concerning cultural locations and all submissions by users are reviewed by the KRB editorial team and included in the Kulturkataster only after a corresponding decision. 

KRB reserves the right to edit, supplement or refrain from publishing data where this is necessary to ensure the quality and reliability of the data. KRB is responsible for the substantive concept, operation and editorial management of the Kulturkataster.

#### 7.2.2 Documentation of Changes

To ensure the traceability and quality of the data collection, KRB documents changes to data in the Kulturkataster. Documentation is carried out within the technical capabilities of the Kulturkataster and serves in particular the internal editorial traceability of data maintenance processes.

##### 7.2.2.1 Logging of Changes

Changes and additions to data as well as other relevant actions in connection with data maintenance are logged in the system. The logging includes in particular information on which changes were made, by which user, and at what time.

##### 7.2.2.2 Change History

The logged changes may be stored in the form of a change history and made traceable for editorial purposes. KRB uses this documentation in particular for quality assurance and for the traceability of data changes.

##### 7.2.2.3 Anonymisation After Account Deletion

If a user account is deleted, the account’s personal data are removed in accordance with data protection requirements. However, the changes stored in the system remain part of the change history, but are no longer associated with an identifiable person.
## Obligations of Users, Warranty, Grant of Rights

### 8.1 Responsibility for Data Submitted Through Contributions

Users are responsible for the data submitted to the Kulturkataster through contributions. This applies in particular to contributions involving data to be newly added or amended and cultural locations to be newly recorded. Users are prohibited from submitting contributions to the Kulturkataster that violate applicable law or infringe third-party rights.

#### 8.1.1 Accuracy of Submitted Data

Users ensure that the data they submit are accurate and complete to the best of their knowledge. In particular, it is not permitted to submit data that are knowingly or grossly negligently inaccurate or misleading.

#### 8.1.2 Authorisation to Use the Submitted Data (Disclosure to Third Parties, Publication, etc.)

Users ensure that they are authorised to disclose and publish the data they submit. This also applies in particular to data that are subject to statutory confidentiality provisions, especially the protection of trade secrets, or that must be treated confidentially on the basis of contractual agreements. Users may submit such data to the Kulturkataster only if they are authorised to disclose and pass them on.

Users ensure that, when submitted to the Kulturkataster, data are free from third-party rights and do not infringe any statutory rights or other legitimate interests of third parties.

### 8.2 Permission

Where users propose data for inclusion in the Kulturkataster, they grant KRB permission to store, structure, edit editorially, link with other data, display in the Kulturkataster, make accessible and keep available for download by users such data within the scope of operating and further developing the Kulturkataster. 

This includes in particular the inclusion of data on cultural locations, their presentation in the digital map application, access by users in accordance with their respective access rights and - to the same extent - provision for download and download by users.

The permission also includes the use of the submitted data by KRB for the purposes of documentation, analysis and further development of the Kulturkataster as well as for evaluations, reports, statistical presentations and publications in connection with cultural policy issues and cultural urban development. For this purpose, the data may in particular be aggregated, evaluated and published in an appropriate form or transmitted to competent public bodies.

### 8.3 Warranty, Indemnification

By submitting the data, users warrant that use of the data by KRB to the extent described above does not violate statutory confidentiality provisions, in particular the protection of trade secrets, or contractual confidentiality obligations, and does not otherwise infringe any rights or legitimate interests of third parties. 

This includes in particular that the submitted data do not disseminate inaccurate or misleading information about companies or institutions that would infringe their corporate personality rights or violate provisions of unfair competition law.

Users indemnify KRB against all third-party claims asserted on the basis of data that users have entered into the Kulturkataster or whose inclusion they have proposed, provided that these claims are based on a breach of the obligations set out in Section 5.1.

The indemnification includes in particular claims arising from the infringement of third-party rights, including claims under the protection of trade secrets, contractual confidentiality obligations, corporate personality rights and provisions of unfair competition law.
## Procedure in the Event of Legal Infringements

### 9.1 Reporting Legal Infringements

Persons or institutions that believe their rights are infringed by data published in the Kulturkataster may notify KRB using the contact options provided for this purpose in the Kulturkataster. The report should contain a description of the affected data that is as precise as possible as well as a justification of the alleged legal infringement.

### 9.2 KRB Review Procedure

KRB reviews notices of possible legal infringements within the scope of its editorial responsibility. For this purpose, KRB may in particular request additional data from the reporting persons or from users who submitted the relevant data. During the review, KRB may temporarily restrict the visibility of the affected data to the extent this appears necessary to avoid possible legal infringements.

### 9.3 Notice-and-Takedown Procedure

KRB is not obliged to review all content submitted by users for possible legal infringements before publication. However, if KRB receives a specific notice that data may infringe third-party rights or violate statutory provisions, KRB will review the notice within the scope of its editorial responsibility.

#### 9.3.1 Content of the Notice and Possible Measures

The notice should identify the relevant data as precisely as possible and set out the alleged legal infringement in a comprehensible manner. Where this appears necessary for the review, KRB may
##### 9.3.1.1 Temporarily Restrict the Visibility of the Relevant Data,
##### 9.3.1.2 Request Additional Data from the Users Involved, or
##### 9.3.1.3 Take Further Appropriate Measures to Prevent a Possible Legal Infringement.

#### 9.3.2 Consequences of an Established Legal Infringement

If the review shows that a legal infringement has occurred, KRB may in particular
##### 9.3.2.1 Delete or Correct the Relevant Data,
##### 9.3.2.2 Restrict Publication, or
##### 9.3.2.3 Temporarily or Permanently Block User Accounts.
## Liability

### 10.1 Liability of Users

Users are themselves responsible for the contributions they submit. In particular, they warrant that the submitted data are accurate, do not infringe third-party rights and do not violate statutory provisions.

### 10.2 Liability of KRB

KRB manages the Kulturkataster editorially. KRB reviews and decides on the publication of data submitted by users through contributions. Nevertheless, a complete review of the accuracy, completeness and legal admissibility of all data cannot be guaranteed. Insofar as KRB processes data submitted by users, it is liable for such third-party data in accordance with statutory provisions.

#### 10.2.1 The statutory liability limitations for hosting services apply to the storage and making available of data provided by users, in particular under the German Digital Services Act (Digitale-Dienste-Gesetz) and Regulation (EU) 2022/2065. The foregoing limitation of liability also does not apply to content that KRB itself creates, researches or is responsible for in terms of content.
KRB gives no warranty for the continuing accuracy, completeness and up-to-dateness of all data submitted by users.
## Deletion Requests by Cultural Organizations

### 11.1 Right to Deletion

Cultural locations affected by published data may request from KRB the deletion of data or restriction of their visibility to the extent that their publication infringes legally protected rights.

#### 11.1.1 Trade Secrets

A claim for removal or restriction of visibility may be asserted in particular if data are made publicly accessible that constitute trade secrets within the meaning of statutory provisions and whose disclosure was unauthorised. To the extent that corresponding data were entered into the Kulturkataster by users, a claim is initially directed against the person who entered the data. 

Responsibility of KRB as operator of the Kulturkataster comes into consideration in particular if KRB obtains knowledge of possible unauthorised disclosure and nevertheless continues to keep the relevant data publicly accessible.

#### 11.1.2 Inaccurate or Reputation-Damaging Information

A deletion claim may also exist if published data are inaccurate or are capable of infringing legitimate interests of an organization, in particular its corporate personality rights or protected positions under unfair competition law.

### 11.2 Procedure

Notices of possible legal infringements or deletion requests may be communicated to KRB using the contact options provided in the Kulturkataster. The notice should identify the relevant data as precisely as possible and provide reasons for the alleged legal infringement.

After receiving such a notice, KRB reviews the alleged circumstances within the scope of its editorial responsibility. Where necessary for this purpose, KRB may request additional data from the reporting organization or from users who submitted the relevant data.

If the notice provides sufficient indications of a possible legal infringement, KRB may temporarily restrict the visibility of the affected data until the review has been completed. If a legal infringement is established, KRB may in particular delete, correct or otherwise adapt the data.
## Term and Termination of Use for Users
### 12.1 Use of the Kulturkataster via a registered account is made possible for an indefinite period.
### 12.2  Termination by Notice
Users may terminate their account at any time without giving reasons. Termination may take place in particular through the corresponding function within the account or by notifying KRB.

KRB may terminate the user agreement by ordinary notice with a notice period of 30 days.

In these cases, KRB may temporarily or permanently block or delete the relevant account.

### 12.3 Following Termination

After termination of use, the relevant account is deleted. Personal data assigned exclusively to the user account are deleted in accordance with data protection requirements.

Data submitted by users and incorporated by KRB into the Kulturkataster may remain in the Kulturkataster’s data set even after an account has been deleted, provided that their storage and publication are necessary for the operation and documentation of the Kulturkataster and no statutory deletion claims conflict with this.

The change processes documented in the system may continue to exist in anonymised form for reasons of traceability and quality assurance.
## Changes to the Terms of Use

Changes may not alter the fundamental structure of the user relationship or unreasonably disadvantage users.

### 13.2 Information, Consent and Entry Into Force

KRB informs registered users of planned changes to the Terms of Use in good time before they enter into force, in an appropriate form by notice in the user account or by email.
Upon the next login after information about the changes has been provided, registered users are asked to consent to them.

### 13.3 If consent is not given, the account can no longer be used. Users are free to terminate their use of the Kulturkataster at any time in accordance with Section 9 of these Terms of Use.

### 14.2 Further information (right of access, rectification, withdrawal of consent, erasure, etc.) can be found in KRB’s Privacy Policy at [https://dsgvo-info.cortina-consult.de/kulturkataster-en/](https://dsgvo-info.cortina-consult.de/kulturkataster-en/).
